Based on the clinical guidelines provided, there is no specific recommendation from the US Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) regarding how often women aged 40 to 74 should get a screening mammogram. The USPSTF does not currently recommend annual mammograms for this age group but emphasizes biennial screening for women within this age range [USPSTF Breast Cancer Screening Recommendation, 2024]. 

For other aspects of colorectal cancer screening, the USPSTF recommends starting at age 45 with options including colonoscopy every 10 years, annual fecal immunochemical test (FIT), or stool DNA testing every 1-3 years [USPSTF Colorectal Cancer Screening Recommendation, 2021].

Since there isn’t a specific guideline for breast cancer screening in this age group, it’s important to consult the latest clinical guidelines from organizations such as the American Cancer Society (ACS) for more tailored recommendations. Always discuss your individual risk factors and preferences with your healthcare provider.

results.content: The USPSTF recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 to 74 years. Evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of screening in women 75 years and older.
The USPSTF recommends screening for colorectal cancer in all adults aged 45 to 75 years. Screening options include colonoscopy every 10 years, annual FIT testing, or stool DNA-FIT every 1-3 years.
